PART I

Item 1. Business

Example Corp designs and sells industrial widgets and a subscription software platform used to monitor widget fleets. The company operates in two segments, Hardware and Software, and sells through direct sales and distributors in North America, Europe and Asia. Software subscriptions grew to represent a larger share of revenue during the year.

Our widget fleet monitoring platform competes with offerings from larger industrial automation vendors. We believe our integrated hardware and software approach, installed base and service network are competitive advantages.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Our business is subject to numerous risks. Supply chain disruptions could delay widget production because several critical components, including specialty sensors, are available from a single supplier located in one region.

We face intense competition and pricing pressure from larger competitors with greater resources, which could reduce our market share and gross margin. New export control regulations may restrict sales to certain customers.

Cybersecurity incidents affecting our monitoring platform could expose customer data, damage our reputation and result in litigation and regulatory penalties. Our insurance may not cover all such losses.

Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments

None.

Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Overview. Total revenue increased 12% year over year to $4.2 billion, driven by 31% growth in Software subscriptions, partially offset by a 3% decline in Hardware revenue as customers delayed capital spending.

Gross margin expanded to 46.5% from 44.1% due to the favorable mix shift toward Software. Operating expenses rose 8% as we invested in research and development and expanded our sales force in Europe.

Liquidity and Capital Resources. We ended the year with $1.1 billion of cash and equivalents. Net cash provided by operating activities was $780 million. During the year we repurchased $300 million of common stock and repaid $150 million of term debt. We believe existing cash and cash flow will be sufficient to fund operations.

Outlook. For next fiscal year we expect revenue growth in the high single digits, with Software growth above 20%.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

We are exposed to foreign currency risk, primarily the euro and yen, and to interest rate risk on our variable rate term loan. A hypothetical 10% change in exchange rates would change annual revenue by approximately $90 million.
